passages.quote: def Language : Type := List Bool → Prop

structure NPCertificate (P : (List Bool → List Bool → Bool) → Prop) (L : Language) where
  witnessBound : Polynomial ℕ
  check : List Bool → List Bool → Bool
  check_polyTime : P check
  spec : ∀ x : List Bool, L x ↔
    ∃ w : List Bool, w.length ≤ witnessBound.eval x.length ∧ check x w = true

def InNP (P : (List Bool → List Bool → Bool) → Prop) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (NPCertificate P L)

def PolyTimeRel (R : List Bool → List Bool → Bool) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime encodePair encodeBool (fun p => R p.1 p.2))
abbrev ProofOracle : Type := ℕ → Bool

inductive QueryTree : ℕ → Type
  | leaf {d : ℕ} (accept : Bool) : QueryTree d
  | query {d : ℕ} (addr : ℕ) (onFalse onTrue : QueryTree d) : QueryTree (d + 1)

def eval : {d : ℕ} → QueryTree d → ProofOracle → Bool
  | _, .leaf b, _ => b
  | _, .query a f t, π => if π a then (t.eval π) else (f.eval π)

def addresses : {d : ℕ} → QueryTree d → Finset ℕ
  | _, .leaf _ => ∅
  | _, .query a f t => insert a (f.addresses ∪ t.addresses)

structure Verifier where
  randomness : ℕ → ℕ
  queries : ℕ
  run : (x : List Bool) → Fin (2 ^ randomness x.length) → QueryTree queries

def acceptingRandomness : Finset (Fin (2 ^ V.randomness x.length)) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun r => (V.run x r).eval π = true)

def accProb : ℚ :=
  ((V.acceptingRandomness x π).card : ℚ) / ((2 : ℚ) ^ V.randomness x.length)
def CompleteAt : Prop := ∃ π : ProofOracle, V.accProb x π = 1
def SoundAt (s : ℚ) : Prop := ∀ π : ProofOracle, V.accProb x π ≤ s

def ReadsBelow (N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, ∀ a ∈ (V.run x r).addresses, a < N

def CanonicalRandomness (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, V.randomness n = a * Nat.clog 2 (n + 2) + b
abbrev VerifierAlg : Type := List Bool → List Bool → List Bool → Bool ⊕ ℕ

theorem np_subset_pcp (L : Language) (hL : InNP Machine.PolyTimeRel L) :
    ∃ (V : Verifier) (alg : VerifierAlg) (a b q : ℕ) (p : Polynomial ℕ),
      Machine.PolyTimeAlg alg ∧
      V.ImplementedBy alg ∧
      V.queries = q ∧
      V.CanonicalRandomness a b ∧
      (∀ x : List Bool, V.ReadsBelow x (p.eval x.length)) ∧
      (∀ x : List Bool, L x → V.CompleteAt x) ∧
      (∀ x : List Bool, ¬ L x → V.SoundAt x (1 / 2))
A language is a predicate on bit strings.

A certificate that L is in NP consists
of a polynomial bound p, a checking relation `check` that is polynomial-time in
the sense `P`, and a proof of the usual equivalence: x ∈ L if and only if some
witness w with |w| ≤ p(|x|) is accepted.

The notion of polynomial time is a
parameter here. The main theorem fixes it to the concrete machine model below.

`Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime` is Mathlib's definition: a finite multi-stack
Turing machine computes the function, and halts within q(n) steps for a fixed
polynomial q, where n is the length of the encoded input.

The input pair (x, w)
is written on the tape as x, a separator symbol, then w.
A proof is an infinite bit string π : ℕ → {0,1}.

A `QueryTree d` is an adaptive
decision tree of depth at most d: each internal node reads one proof bit and
branches on it, and each leaf accepts or rejects.

A verifier specifies how many
random bits it uses on inputs of length n, a bound on the number of queries, and
for each input x and each random string r ∈ {0, …, 2<sup>randomness(|x|)</sup> − 1}
the tree it runs.

`accProb` is the exact fraction of random strings on which V accepts x with
  proof π.
`CompleteAt x`: some proof is accepted with probability 1.

`SoundAt x s`:
  every proof is accepted with probability at most s.

`ReadsBelow x N`: on input x, no tree ever queries an address ≥ N, whatever
  the random string and the answers. This is how "a proof of length N" is
  expressed.

`CanonicalRandomness a b`: the verifier uses *exactly* a⌈log₂(n+2)⌉ + b random
  bits. An upper bound would be too weak: the randomness function is an
  arbitrary function of n, and an upper bound would let it encode an arbitrary
  (even uncomputable) predicate of the input length, which the verifier could
  read off from how many random bits it receives.

A `Verifier` is a mathematical object: a family of decision trees. Its
efficiency is certified separately, by an algorithm.

Given the input x, the
random string r as bits, and the answers received so far, `alg` either halts
with a decision (`Bool`) or names the next proof address to query (`ℕ`).

`ImplementedBy` says that unfolding `alg` reproduces exactly the tree
`V.run x r`, for every x and r.

`PolyTimeAlg` says `alg` runs in polynomial time
on Mathlib's Turing machines.
Let L ⊆ {0,1}* be a language in NP.
Then there are a verifier V, an algorithm, constants a, b, q and a polynomial p, all chosen before any input x, such that:
the algorithm runs in polynomial time,
and it computes exactly V;
V reads at most q proof bits;
on inputs of length n, V uses exactly a⌈log₂(n+2)⌉ + b random bits;
on input x, V reads only the first p(\|x\|) bits of the proof;
if x ∈ L, some proof is accepted with probability 1;
if x ∉ L, every proof is accepted with probability at most 1/2.

That is NP ⊆ PCP(O(log n), O(1)), with perfect completeness and a
polynomial-time verifier.
`(L : Language) (hL : InNP Machine.PolyTimeRel L)`
`∃ (V : Verifier) (alg : VerifierAlg) (a b q : ℕ) (p : Polynomial ℕ),`
`Machine.PolyTimeAlg alg ∧`
`V.ImplementedBy alg ∧`
`V.queries = q ∧`
`V.CanonicalRandomness a b ∧`
`(∀ x : List Bool, V.ReadsBelow x (p.eval x.length)) ∧`
`(∀ x : List Bool, L x → V.CompleteAt x) ∧`
`(∀ x : List Bool, ¬ L x → V.SoundAt x (1 / 2))`

plain.PCP.Verifier.ImplementedBy: Match the algorithm to the tree

PCP.Verifier.ImplementedBy.text: The left side unfolds alg with budget V.queries. In QueryTree.ofStep, a request for a further query at budget zero becomes a rejecting leaf (CostModel.lean, lines 42 to 44), so the equation compares V.run x r with this capped unfolding. The doc comment at lines 38 to 40 speaks of halting within q queries; in the definition, an algorithm that has not halted in time rejects.

PCP.Verifier.ReadsBelow.text: QueryTree.addresses (Definition.lean, lines 47 to 49) collects the address of every query node on both branches. So ReadsBelow bounds every branch of every tree, including a branch that asks the same address twice and takes different answers, which no single proof produces. This agrees with the guide's "whatever the random string and the answers".

PCP.QueryTree.ofStep.text: The guide calls this unfolding alg. In detail, it starts from the answers so far and a budget d. While d is positive, a halt gives a leaf and a request for address a gives a query node at a, continuing with d − 1 on each answer. At d = 0 a request gives a rejecting leaf.

PCP.bitsOfFin.text: The guide calls this the random string r as bits. It writes the index r as exactly k bits, least significant bit first, so every random string handed to alg has length k.

PCP.Machine.encodeTriple.text: The guide has no sentence on this helper. The machine's input is x, a separator, the random bits, a separator, then the answers so far.

PCP.Machine.encodeAnswer.text: The guide has no sentence on this helper. A decision is written as one bit; a query is a separator followed by the address in binary (Nat.bits).

PCP.Machine.encodeBool.text: The guide has no sentence on this helper. A Boolean result is written as a single bit.

PCP.Machine.ofBits.text: The guide has no sentence on this helper. Each bit becomes one tape symbol, in order, with no separators.

PCP.Machine.Sym.text: The guide has no sentence on this type. A tape cell holds a bit or the separator that marks where one argument ends.

PCP.np_subset_pcp.text: The guide's line-by-line table gives one row for each part of the Lean statement, in order, and each row says what that part says. The notes on ImplementedBy and ReadsBelow give the exact reading of two rows.
